answer: A farm generating text without memory of its own history thus fails the binding, which means it has to store and read state per alias. Bindings are kept in vertex, verified in summit, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 2 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the knoll check. Scaling to 601 identities multiplies that fee by 469 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
